entries.content:
## Delta

Yes. Your run built the desktop app and launched it with the deterministic runtime, and its log shows the app working through Tauri's own channel:

- **Startup:** the webview loaded and requested the session, patients, cases and conversations. SurrealDB 3.3.0 opened its store under `~/Library/Application Support/ai.prometheusags.patientgpt/`.
- **19:47:15 — a `start_run`:** someone sent a message from the window. The `list_conversations` calls right after it suggest the new conversation was then re-listed, which is what happens once a run is saved.
- **19:47:24 and 19:47:42:** `list_cases` and `list_conversations` bursts, which look like moving between patients or cases.
- **Port 5173:** Vite started on `localhost:5173` even though the OrbStack container holds the wildcard address, so no override was needed.

The log only shows which commands ran, not what appeared on screen. It's still unconfirmed:

- whether the 40px title bar shows with the PatientGPT mark, and nothing overlaps it;
- whether the reply streamed in and the new conversation appeared under History;
- whether the conversation is still there after you quit and run `cargo tauri dev` again (the SurrealDB persistence check).

Two things in the log are worth fixing:

- **Duplicate calls at startup:** `session` and `list_patients` each run four times. That was reported before and is still not diagnosed. It's probably more than one hook or StrictMode registering the same fetch.
- **RocksDB memory sizing:** SurrealDB sized its block cache at 33 GB from your machine's 37.5 GB total. That's a ceiling rather than memory actually in use, but a desktop app shouldn't default to claiming nearly all of RAM. It should be capped in `patient-gpt-storage` when the store opens.

Can you tell me what the window showed? Specifically: whether the title bar looked right, whether the reply appeared, and whether the conversation was still there after a restart. If you send a screenshot I'll compare it against the brand board.

## Delta

PatientGPT is scaffolded across all three surfaces on one shared Rust core, following the `docs/design` tokens and brand. Everything builds and passes static checks. I saw the web app working end to end myself. Only part of the desktop and mobile behaviour has been observed. No tests were run (the project runs tests only at the end of a phase), and nothing is committed.

| Surface | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Rust core | **Passed** | `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` are clean. Every server route answered `curl` correctly, including bad input. |
| Web (React, PGlite) | **Passed (local)** | `pnpm build` passes. I loaded it against the live Rust server: the greeting, sidebar and "Due next" rows rendered, and a chip streamed the reply into History. |
| Flutter | **Passed on simulator only** | `flutter analyze` is clean. In a debug run on the iPhone 17 simulator, the home view showed data from Rust through the bridge, with HTTP pointed at a dead port. |
| Tauri desktop | **Build-only** | It builds, launches, serves all six commands through Tauri, and opens SurrealDB 3.3.0. Every window screenshot came back blank, so the titlebar, a streamed reply and persistence across a restart were not seen. |
| iOS/Android/Tauri release builds | **Blocked** | The project's tier gate blocks these until the KBD phase advances. I left the gate in place. |

All three surfaces use one token source, `assets/templates/design-tokens/tokens.toml`. Its output matches all 60 light and 42 dark values in the prototype. There is no `docs/branding` folder; the brand assets in `docs/design/brand/` were used.

**Where the Praxis standard was overridden:** `docs/design` wins on palette, fonts, layout and navigation, and your contract wins on desktop storage. The full table is in `docs/plan/scaffold-plan.md`.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Desktop storage:** Praxis requires pglite-oxide; your contract says SurrealDB 3.3.0. I followed the contract.
- **Holding SurrealDB at 3.3.0:** `=3.3.0` in `Cargo.toml` doesn't hold its sub-crates. Only `Cargo.lock` keeps them at 3.3.0, and a `cargo update` would quietly move them to 3.3.4. You'd need to commit the lockfile or pin the sub-crates directly.
- **Pins:** the new pins need adding to `versions.toml` by hand. One differs from plan: `build_runner` is 2.16.2, because 2.17.1 conflicts with `riverpod_generator`.
- **Copy:** about 20 new error and loading lines, which the prototype doesn't have, need your review.

**Known defects:**
- Sidebar dates are clipped ("Oct" instead of "Oct 3").
- The wrong patient opens first. The prototype opens the first one due.
- The desktop transport shows errors as `[object Object]` and retries even permanent errors such as "not found".
- When the server serves the built web app, unknown `/api/*` paths return the page instead of a 404.

**Contract gaps:** the stage track, the "Next:" line and the short procedure names need fields the frozen contract doesn't have. The synthetic due dates also read as overdue, because they're counted from today rather than the prototype's fixed date.

The plan and contracts are in `docs/plan/scaffold-plan.md` and `docs/plan/scaffold-contracts.md`. The Praxis extract is in `docs/plan/reference/praxis-ui-standard-extract.md`.

## Delta

All five defects are fixed. The server build, clippy on the server and desktop crates, and the web build are all clean. I checked four of the fixes in the browser or with `curl`. The desktop error mapping only compiles so far: nothing has run in a live desktop window.

**Clipped sidebar dates.** The sidebar's lists were sizing themselves to the longest procedure name (390px inside a 252px sidebar), which pushed every date off the right edge. I limited them to the sidebar's width in `web/src/styles/shell.css`. At 1100px the patient dates now show in full ("Oct 3", "Oct 12"), long case names end in an ellipsis with their date still visible, and the sidebar no longer scrolls sideways.

**First-due patient.** The sidebar picked which patient to open as soon as patients loaded, before every patient's cases had arrived, so the order was still changing. It now waits until each patient's cases are in. Delgado, the earliest due, now opens on load. The fix is in `use-patient-directory.ts` and `use-sidebar-nav.ts`.

**Tauri error mapping and retries.** Desktop errors now keep the host's `code` and `message`, and the HTTP side reads its error body the same way. Errors about bad input or a missing record now fail at once instead of retrying.
- In the browser: opening an unknown patient showed "The PatientGPT server answered 404: patient `nobody` not found" within two seconds, and the request was not retried three times.
- The desktop path has the same logic but has only been type-checked.

**Host top inset.** The web app now has a `--host-inset-top` variable in `web/src/styles/app.css`. It moves the app, the scrim, the phone drawer, the Files and canvas overlays, and the focused skip link down by that amount. The desktop title bar sets it to 40px and is now `position: fixed`, so it no longer overrides any of the web app's layout classes.
- With 40px applied at 375px wide, the app, scrim and drawer all run from 40px to 760px.
- Fixing this exposed two smaller problems, both fixed:
  - the phone drawer's `height: 100%` ran 40px past the bottom of the screen;
  - the hidden skip link peeked out under the bar, because the browser doesn't update an in-progress animation when the variable changes. Now only its focused position moves; when focused it sits at 48px.
- How it looks in the actual desktop window hasn't been checked; the earlier window screenshots came back blank.

**`/api` fallback.** When the server also serves the built web app, any unknown `/api` path now returns a JSON 404 instead of the HTML page, for example `{"code":"not_found","message":"no API route at /api/nope"}`. App routes such as `/p/kaminski` still load the page. The fix is in `crates/patient-gpt-server/src/lib.rs`.
